packets.title: Swift Vapor precision: no double slash (`app.get("/users")` reads `GET /users`, not `GET //users`), a client call with a trailing closure (`client.post("https://..") { }`) mints no ROUTE, `app.get(use: index)` mints `GET /`, and grouped builders join their prefix
packets.area: FD per-language precision: Swift (§E W2 DH.20)
packets.rationale: §E W2 (DH.20): 'a client call with a trailing closure mints a phantom `POST /https://...` ROUTE; `app.get("/users")` reads `GET //users`; `app.get(use: index)` mints no `GET /`; grouped builders (`app.grouped("users")`) do not join the prefix'. Re-verified at HEAD 37fb9384 on a probe package: ROUTE `GET //users` and ROUTE `POST /https://api.example.com/x` (from `client.post("https://api.example.com/x") { req in }` inside a function, not a router). These are false nodes on any Vapor server.
entry_points: parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs - the Vapor route reader (DH.20's `use:` / trailing-closure rule): path components joined with single `/` (a component that already starts with `/` is not prefixed again); the receiver must be a route builder (`app`, `routes`, a `RoutesBuilder`-typed parameter, or a var assigned from `.grouped(` / `.group(` of one), never a `Client` / `req.client` / an `http` client; a first argument that is a URL with a scheme (`http://`, `https://`) is never a route path
